paragraphs: Decision center: the work of drywall and ceiling tile installers is to turn these front-end conditions — drawings and design requirements, studs and hangers and substrates and suspension fittings, and panels and acoustic tiles and moisture-proof and insulation materials — into an interior finished product that can be hung, aligned, and held to joint and flatness and safety boundaries: first read the drawings and specifications to determine the installation method and sequence and materials and tools, then measure and lay out and install metal or wood studs and hangers and check the verticality and levelness of the substrate and suspension fittings, then cut and assemble the stud frame and hoist drywall or ceiling panels and secure them with adhesive and nails and screws, then measure and cut openings for outlets, windows, air grilles, ducts, irregular and corner boards and trim the panel edges to keep joints flush, then install window and door and air grille frames and decorative trim and seal the joints between ceiling panels and walls, and finally coordinate joint treatment with the tapers, check the studs and hangers and masonry surfaces and clean up and close out and report anomalies. The point of judgment is not 'can the panel be hung up' but whether every step of the chain — reading drawings, layout and framing, installation, opening and edging, and inspection and coordination — is accurate, verifiable, and handled according to the design and working-at-height and fire protection requirements.

Suitable for a first try: willing to stand and climb for long periods at interior fit-out sites and carry panels and studs; able to work according to drawings and design dimensions and stud specifications and stay careful about flatness and joints and alignment; able to withstand heights and dust and noise and handling and bending and climbing; willing to do layout and inspection and close-out and record keeping and to accept schedule and piece-rate or quota rhythms.

Needs caution: if you expect this job to be in an office or to involve only watching others build, or you are unwilling to wear protective equipment and follow working-at-height and fire protection and electrical and hoisting safety requirements (going up high without a stable platform, closing panels without checking the suspension fittings and substrate, hanging heavy equipment from ceiling studs, not providing expansion joints and not treating joints), or you find it hard to keep precision and patience when carrying panels and repeating alignment under schedule pressure, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Low-risk verification: using the fictional drawings, layout records, stud and hanger layout drawings, and panel lists provided on this page, complete a paper exercise that 'arranges the ceiling and partition framing and panel installation sequence according to the drawings and the room's clear height — writes a paragraph on hanger and main stud and cross stud layout and leveling and reverse bracing according to the stud specifications — and fills in one substrate and suspension fitting inspection and opening and edging and anomaly record', only to verify whether you are willing to check item by item according to the design and specifications and safety requirements and to record truthfully. The exercise uses fictional materials and does not involve real construction sites, heights, or power tools, and it does not constitute a structural or fire protection or construction quality acceptance conclusion, nor is it equivalent to job training or a working-at-height or special operation qualification.

Decision center: whether drawings and design and studs and substrate and suspension fittings can be turned into an installation and inspection chain that the team leader and the tapers and engineering inspection can all take up and verify.

The work is mainly at interior fit-out sites with frequent communication with the team: standing continuously 92%, continuous use of hands 83% (another 17% more than half), continuous contact with others 88%, exposure to heights every day 72% (another 18% weekly or more), continuous walking or running 78%, face-to-face discussions every day 68% (another 26% monthly or more), time pressure every day 52% (another 42% weekly or more), decision freedom 'very large' 54% (another 36% some), precision or accuracy 'extremely important' 37% (another 50% very important), decisions every day 74%, wearing common protective or safety equipment every day 61%, responsibility for the health and safety of others 'very high responsibility' 45% (another 34% high responsibility), competition 'extremely fierce' 43% (another 13% high, 42% moderate), continuous climbing of ladders or scaffolds 47% (another 21% more than half), continuous bending or twisting 52% (another 20% about half), minor burns or cuts every day 34% (another 34% weekly or more), exposure to hazardous equipment 'every day' 20% (another 43% weekly or more), consequences of error 'extremely serious' 30% (another 17% very serious, 26% fairly serious), continuous kneeling, squatting, bending, or crawling 31%, work hours 'regular' 94%, automation level 'not automated at all' 55%.

Similar names do not mean the same duties: this page is O*NET-SOC 47-2081.00 Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers. Adjacent positions have different duties — carpenters handle wood structural framing and doors and windows and formwork; plasterers handle plaster and stucco and finishes; tile and stone setters handle tile and stone laying; insulation workers handle the main body of insulation and soundproofing material installation; brickmasons and blockmasons handle masonry; painters handle wall coating; glaziers handle glass and curtain wall installation; construction laborers handle general site labor. This occupation is set on installing drywall and other wallboard to building ceilings or interior walls, and installing or securing acoustic tiles and vibration-damping materials to ceilings and walls to damp or reflect sound and decorate, and also includes securing wood or metal or rockboard lath to walls and ceilings or partitions as the supporting substrate for plaster or fire protection or acoustic material. Structural safety and fire protection and firefighting and construction quality acceptance and working-at-height qualifications are governed by the regulations and standards and competent authorities of the relevant jurisdiction and this project's requirements, are not inferred from the job title, and must not exceed authorization to issue acceptance-pass, safety, or compliance conclusions externally.

Inputs that must be verified: drawings and design specifications and ceiling or partition construction and the room's clear height and opening elevations, the specifications and spacing and anti-corrosion and fire protection treatment of studs and hangers and suspension fittings and connectors, the specifications and conformity certificates and performance test reports of panels and acoustic tiles and moisture-proof and insulation materials, the verticality and levelness and firmness of the substrate and masonry and embedded parts, working-at-height and temporary power and power tool safety conditions, concealed works and joint and expansion joint requirements, and concealed works and inspection and acceptance record requirements. Things that must not be done: starting work without verifying the drawings and clear height and elevations, working at height without a stable platform or a safety harness, closing panels without checking the firmness and anti-corrosion treatment of suspension fittings and embedded parts and the substrate, installing heavy equipment and equipment with vibration loads directly on ceiling studs, not providing expansion joints and not treating joints and openings, not applying fire protection treatment to wood studs and wood panels per the standards, and concealing or delaying reports of structural anomalies and safety and quality hazards.

The fit judgment should be made by combining whether you can stand and climb for long periods at interior fit-out sites and carry panels, whether you can work according to drawings and design dimensions and stud specifications and stay careful about flatness and joints and alignment, whether you can withstand heights and dust and noise and handling and bending and climbing, whether you can do layout and inspection and close-out and record keeping, and whether you are clear about your duties and authorization and working-at-height and structural safety boundaries; it is not replaced by a self-assessment of being 'strong' or 'knowing how to build'; all of this must be confirmed in supervised actual construction and team observation.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real interior fit-out installation and working at height and fire protection and electrical and structural safety and construction acceptance must be undertaken by organizations and personnel with the corresponding training and qualifications that follow the regulations and standards of the relevant jurisdiction and this project's requirements; individuals must not exceed authorization to issue conclusions on structural safety, fire protection, firefighting, construction quality acceptance, or compliance externally, and this page does not constitute structural, fire protection, firefighting, quality acceptance, or legal advice.

The work object of this occupation is interior fit-out installation sites: drawings and design specifications and ceiling or partition construction and the room's clear height and opening elevations, the specifications of studs and hangers and suspension fittings and connectors, panels and acoustic tiles and moisture-proof and insulation materials, the verticality and levelness and firmness of the substrate and masonry and embedded parts, working-at-height and temporary power and power tool conditions, and concealed works and inspection and acceptance records. The output is installation results and records that meet the design and flatness and joint requirements: studs and hangers and panels and acoustic tiles installed by specification and spacing, openings and expansion joints and joints provided and treated per the design, and verifiable substrate and suspension fitting inspection and concealed works and anomaly reporting and handover records. The basis for judgment is the drawings and design specifications and material and stud specifications and standards and working-at-height safety requirements, not personal habits or the job title.

Judgment one: whether the drawings and design and clear height and elevations are verified clearly — checking against the construction and the room's clear height and opening elevations and the design documents and handover inspection, rather than starting work from impression.

Judgment two: whether the substrate and suspension fittings and embedded parts are firm — checking the firmness, verticality, levelness, and anti-corrosion and fire protection treatment of the substrate and masonry and embedded parts and suspension fittings and connectors, rather than closing panels without checking.

Judgment three: whether stud and hanger specifications and spacing follow the basis — installing studs and hangers and connectors according to the design and standards and controlling spacing and end distances and reverse bracing and transfer layers, rather than laying them out at will.

Judgment four: whether panels and acoustic tiles and openings and edging are in place — installing and securing panels per the design and measuring and cutting openings and irregular and corner boards and trimming panel edges and providing expansion joints, rather than cutting and jointing carelessly.

Judgment five: whether joints and coordination and concealed acceptance are held — coordinating joint treatment with the tapers and completing concealed works and inspection and acceptance records per the standards, rather than skipping concealed inspection.

Judgment six: whether safety and anomalies and handover are held — working per the working-at-height and electrical and hoisting safety requirements and reporting and handing over per the system when structural anomalies or safety hazards or quality problems occur, rather than concealing or delaying.

The work of drywall and ceiling tile installers can be divided into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is drawing reading and layout and framing and substrate: study the drawings and other specifications to determine the installation method and sequence and material and tool requirements, measure and lay out and mark surfaces according to the drawings and details, cut and assemble metal studs to make floor or ceiling frames for the room or corridor locations, install horizontal and vertical metal or wood studs to the framing so wallboard can be secured to interior walls, secure wood or metal or rockboard lath (a gypsum-based lath, not rock wool) to the structural framing of walls and ceilings or partitions as the supporting substrate for plaster or fire protection or acoustic material, install roll insulation between studs and nail a plastic moisture barrier over the insulation, and install metal lath where plaster will be exposed to weather or water or curved or irregular surfaces. The second is installation and fabrication: hoist drywall onto the metal framing of walls and ceilings in offices and schools or other large buildings (adjusting panel height with lifting or hoisting equipment when necessary), position and secure wallboard or drywall with adhesive and nails and screws, measure and cut openings in panels or ceiling tiles for outlets, windows, air grilles, ducts, and other equipment with a keyhole saw or other cutting tool, cut metal or wood studs and trim to size, cut irregular or corner boards to size with a keyhole saw and insert them into the surrounding frame, trim the rough edges of wallboard with a knife to keep joints flush, assemble or install metal frames or decorative trim for windows and doors and air grilles, hang ceiling wires to wall lines to position main studs, suspend angle grid or channel steel from the ceiling with steel wire, install acoustic ceiling tiles or blocks or strips or sheet vibration-damping material to ceilings or walls to reduce sound reflection or decorate rooms, seal the joints between ceiling tiles and walls, and cut ceiling tile edges to fit the wall where no wall line is specified. The third is coordination and inspection and close-out: coordinate work with the tapers who cover drywall joints, inspect the verticality and levelness of suspension fittings and mechanical fasteners and masonry surfaces, nail channel steel or wood furring strips to surfaces to provide an installation substrate for ceiling tiles, secure ceiling tiles and lath directly to the structural framing with adhesive or nails or screws or staples or steel wire, remove existing plaster or drywall or panels with a pry bar and hammer, and record and report anomalies and complete handover. All three work surfaces proceed within the drawings and design specifications and material and stud specifications and standards and working-at-height safety requirements.

Study the drawings and specifications to determine the installation method and sequence and materials and tools → measure and lay out and mark → install metal or wood studs and hangers → install lath substrate and insulation and moisture barrier → check the verticality and levelness of the substrate and suspension fittings

Executable list of construction and sequence and material and tool key points, layout and stud arrangement and leveling records, substrate and suspension fitting inspection and concealed works records

Cut and assemble the stud frame → hoist drywall or ceiling panels and secure with adhesive and nails and screws → measure and cut openings and irregular and corner boards and trim panel edges → install frames and decorative trim and ceiling wires and angle grid → seal ceiling-to-wall joints and install acoustic tiles

Coordination and inspection and close-out

Coordinate joint treatment with the tapers → inspect the studs and suspension fittings and masonry surfaces → remove existing plaster or panels and clean up and close out → record and report anomalies and hand over

Core purpose

Turn drawings and design and studs and substrate and materials into installation results that meet the design and flatness and joint requirements: drawings and clear height clear, substrate and suspension fittings firm, studs and hangers per specification, panels and openings and edging in place, and joints and concealed acceptance held.

Core purposes of adjacent positions: carpentry ensures wood structures and doors and windows and formwork take shape; plastering ensures the substrate and finish are flat and bonded; tile and stone ensure finish laying and drainage and durability; insulation ensures thermal and acoustic performance; masonry ensures load bearing and enclosure; painting ensures the finish coating and appearance.
Main objects and basis

The objects are drawings and design specifications and ceiling or partition construction and the room's clear height and opening elevations, studs and hangers and suspension fittings and connectors, panels and acoustic tiles and moisture-proof and insulation materials, substrate and masonry and embedded parts, and concealed works and inspection and acceptance records; the basis is the drawings and design specifications and material and stud specifications and standards and working-at-height safety requirements.

Objects and basis of adjacent positions: timber and framing and formwork (wood structure codes); mortar and plaster and substrate (plastering process); tile and stone and bonding layer (laying codes); insulation and soundproofing materials (insulation and energy efficiency codes); blocks and mortar (masonry codes); coatings and substrate (painting process).
Core process

Drawing reading and layout and framing and substrate → installation and fabrication (cutting and hoisting and securing and opening and edging and joints) → coordination and inspection and close-out and anomaly reporting.

Carpenters may install wallboard/insulation, plasterers may apply decorative plaster, and hard tile and stone may be laid to walls, floors, and ceilings and the like; the classification emphasis differs, but some actual tasks overlap, so it is not claimed that they are never interchangeable or automatically mutually recognized.
Main outputs

Outputs of adjacent positions: wood structures and doors and windows and formwork and correction records; plastered surfaces and flatness and bonding records; tile and stone surfaces and grouting and hollowing records; insulation and soundproofing layers and securing records; masonry and mortar and verticality records; coating films and appearance and adhesion records.
Responsible parties

This occupation bears execution responsibility for installing studs and hangers and panels and acoustic tiles according to drawings and specifications and handling openings and joints and edging; responsibility for structural safety and fire protection and firefighting acceptance and construction quality acceptance is borne by the design unit and construction unit and competent authorities and personnel with the corresponding qualifications according to regulations and standards.

Responsibilities of adjacent positions: wood structures and doors and windows are borne by carpenters and their organizations; plastering and finishes are borne by plasterers and their organizations; tile and stone laying is borne by the setters and their organizations; insulation is borne by insulation workers and their organizations; masonry is borne by masons and their organizations; painting is borne by painters and their organizations.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with the team leader and the tapers and carpenters and water and electricity and HVAC and in-ceiling equipment installation and inspection, and adjust priorities according to the operation sequencing and schedule and concealed acceptance milestones; immediately report structural anomalies and safety hazards and quality problems and matters beyond authorization.

Collaboration of adjacent positions: carpentry interfaces with plumbing and electrical and decoration; plastering interfaces with water and electricity provisions and decoration; tile and stone interfaces with waterproofing and water and electricity; insulation interfaces with enclosure and equipment; masonry interfaces with structure and plumbing and electrical provisions; painting interfaces with substrate and decoration.

In this job, which judgments are most prone to error, and how should they be verified?

Common errors cluster in four areas: first, starting work without verifying the drawings and clear height and elevations, resulting in the ceiling elevation and openings and clear height not matching and rework; second, closing panels without checking the firmness and anti-corrosion treatment of the substrate and suspension fittings and embedded parts, resulting in sagging and falling off and safety hazards; third, improper stud and hanger specifications and spacing and reverse bracing, resulting in ceiling deformation and cracked joints and insufficient load capacity; fourth, missing panels and openings and joints and edging and concealed acceptance, resulting in unacceptable appearance and quality and untraceability. This table compares 'drywall and ceiling tile installers' row by row with six adjacent positions that are easily confused within the same building interior fit-out and decoration content or have rotation and transfer relationships, by core work and outputs, key differences, and selection basis. The purpose of the comparison is not to rank them but to explain their respective duty boundaries and authorization scopes — in particular, structural safety determination authority, fire protection and firefighting acceptance authority, construction quality acceptance determination authority, and safety and compliance conclusions cannot be assumed by this occupation as well.

The comparison should rest on three things: first, the work object (timber and framing and formwork, mortar and plaster and substrate, tile and stone and bonding layer, insulation and soundproofing materials, blocks and mortar, coatings and substrate); second, the basis and authorization (the respective application of drawings and design specifications and material and stud specifications and standards and working-at-height safety requirements, wood structure codes, plastering process, laying codes, insulation and energy efficiency codes, masonry codes, and painting process); third, outputs and responsibility (who is responsible for installing studs and panels and acoustic tiles and openings and joints, who is responsible for wood structures and doors and windows, who is responsible for plaster finishes, who is responsible for tile and stone laying, who is responsible for insulation and soundproofing, who is responsible for masonry, and who is responsible for painting). When the three are inconsistent, the actual duties of the position and the design documents and qualification and standard documents prevail.

The selection basis can follow three lines: if you want to install studs and drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles according to drawings at interior fit-out sites and handle openings and joints, this page's occupation is the closest fit; if you want to do adjacent operations such as wood structures or plastering or tile and stone or insulation, carpenter or plasterer or tile and stone setter or insulation worker are adjacent paths; if you want to do masonry or painting, brickmason and blockmason or painter are another path. When transferring positions, what needs to be filled in is material and process and tool knowledge and standard and qualification requirements, not just proficiency.

Build and install wood structural framing and doors and windows and formwork and wood components according to drawings, responsible for cutting and installation and correction and securing.

The object and process differ: carpenters focus on timber and framing and doors and windows and formwork under wood structure codes; this page's occupation focuses on metal or wood studs and paper-faced drywall and acoustic tiles and ceiling construction under drawings and stud and material specifications and working-at-height requirements. The materials, tools, and processes differ and cannot be interchanged by name.

If you want to do wood structures and doors and windows and formwork, you can choose the carpenter direction and check the corresponding training requirements; if you want to do interior drywall and ceiling installation, this page's occupation is the closest fit.

Apply plaster and stucco and finishes to substrates and ensure flatness and bonding and finishing, responsible for substrate preparation and troweling and curing.

The process and materials differ: plasterers focus on mortar and plaster and substrate preparation and finishing; this page's occupation focuses on installing studs and panels and acoustic tiles and treating openings and joints, and plastering is carried out on the lath substrate they install or other substrates. The processes connect but the duties and outputs differ.
If you want to do plastering and finishes, you can choose the plasterer direction; if you want to do panel and ceiling installation, this page's occupation is more suitable.

The object and deliverable differ: tile and stone setters focus on tile and stone and the bonding layer and grouting; this page's occupation focuses on installing drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles and joints and edging (it may include securing tile and lath to framing as a substrate), and the finish method and acceptance basis differ.
If you want to do tile and stone laying, you can choose the tile and stone setter direction; if you want to do stud and panel and ceiling installation, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Insulation workers (47-2131.00)

The object and performance target differ: insulation workers focus on insulation and soundproofing materials and thermal and acoustic performance; this page's occupation installs roll insulation and a moisture barrier between studs as only one link, and the core is the installation of studs and panels and acoustic tiles and flatness and joints.
If you want to lay insulation and soundproofing materials, you can choose the insulation worker direction; if you want to do panel and ceiling installation, this page's occupation is more suitable.

The object and process differ: brickmasons and blockmasons focus on laying bricks and blocks and mortar and grouting as a load-bearing and enclosure masonry operation; this page's occupation is an interior fit-out installation operation that installs studs and panels on existing structures and masonry and does not take on masonry or load-bearing duties.
If you want to do masonry, you can choose the brickmason and blockmason direction; if you want to do interior drywall and ceiling installation, this page's occupation is the closest fit.
Painting and maintenance workers (47-2141.00)

The duties and process differ: painters focus on substrate preparation and coating application and appearance and adhesion, usually after panel and joint treatment is complete; this page's occupation focuses on installing studs and panels and acoustic tiles and joints and edging and does not take on final surface coating and appearance delivery duties.
If you want to do wall painting, you can choose the painting and maintenance worker direction; if you want to do stud and panel installation, this page's occupation is more suitable.

All materials are fictional and contain no real project or structural information unrelated to you.
Portfolio task

Within 40 minutes, arrange the ceiling and partition framing and panel installation sequence according to the drawings and the room's clear height, write a paragraph on hanger and main stud and cross stud arrangement and leveling and reverse bracing according to the stud specifications, and fill in one substrate and suspension fitting inspection and opening and edging and anomaly record.

entries.answer: Study the drawings and other specifications to determine the installation method and sequence and material and tool requirements, measure and lay out and mark surfaces according to the drawings and details, cut and assemble metal studs to make floor or ceiling frames for the room or corridor locations, install horizontal and vertical metal or wood studs to the framing so wallboard can be secured to interior walls, secure wood or metal or rock wool lath to the structural framing of walls and ceilings or partitions as the supporting substrate for plaster or fire protection or acoustic material, and install roll insulation between studs and nail a plastic moisture barrier; hoist drywall onto the metal framing of building walls and ceilings and secure it with adhesive and nails and screws, measure and cut openings in panels or tiles for outlets, windows, air grilles, and ducts with a keyhole saw or other tool, cut metal or wood studs and trim to size, cut irregular or corner boards to size with a keyhole saw and insert them into the surrounding frame, trim the rough edges of wallboard with a knife to keep joints flush, assemble or install metal frames or decorative trim for windows and doors and air grilles, hang ceiling wires to wall lines to position main studs, suspend angle grid or channel steel from the ceiling with steel wire, install acoustic tiles or blocks or strips or sheet vibration-damping material to ceilings or walls to damp or reflect sound or decorate rooms, and seal the joints between ceiling tiles and walls; coordinate work with the tapers who cover drywall joints, inspect the verticality and levelness of suspension fittings and mechanical fasteners and masonry surfaces, nail channel steel or wood furring strips to surfaces to provide an installation substrate for tiles, and remove existing plaster or drywall or panels with a pry bar and hammer and clean up and close out and report anomalies.
entries.question: What does a drywall and ceiling tile installer do on a typical day?

entries.answer: This page's occupation installs metal or wood studs and paper-faced drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles indoors according to drawings and handles openings and joints and edging; carpenters build wood structural framing and doors and windows and formwork; plasterers apply plaster and stucco and finish substrates. description.text: Drywall and ceiling tile installers (O*NET-SOC 47-2081.00) install drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles at building interior fit-out sites: they study the drawings and specifications and measure and lay out and mark, install metal or wood studs and hangers and lath substrate and insulation and moisture barrier, cut and assemble stud frames, hoist and secure drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles, measure and cut openings and irregular and corner boards and trim panel edges and provide expansion joints and seal joints, and coordinate joint treatment with the tapers and inspect suspension fittings and masonry surfaces and clean up and close out. subject.summary: Drywall and ceiling tile installers (U.S. side O*NET-SOC 47-2081.00, Drywall and Ceiling Tile Installers) are the drywall and ceiling panel installation positions in building interior fit-out: they install paper-faced drywall or other wallboard to building ceilings or interior walls and install or secure acoustic tiles or blocks or strips or sheet vibration-damping material to ceilings and walls to damp or reflect sound and decorate rooms, and also secure wood or metal or rock wool lath to walls and ceilings or partitions as the supporting substrate for plaster or fire protection or acoustic material; the work includes studying the drawings and specifications to determine the installation method and sequence and materials and tools, measuring and laying out and marking according to the drawings, installing metal or wood studs and hangers and lath substrate and insulation and moisture barrier, cutting and assembling stud frames, hoisting and securing drywall and ceiling panels and acoustic tiles, measuring and cutting openings for outlets and windows and air grilles and ducts and irregular and corner boards and trimming panel edges and providing expansion joints, installing frames and decorative trim and ceiling wires and angle grid, sealing ceiling-to-wall joints, coordinating joint treatment with the tapers, inspecting the verticality and levelness of suspension fittings and mechanical fasteners and masonry surfaces, and removing existing plaster or panels and cleaning up and closing out. U.S. definition: the BLS 2025 wage data median is 58,930 USD per year (28.33 USD per hour), with annual percentiles of 38,460 / 47,440 / 58,930 / 74,230 / 102,010 USD (hourly percentiles 18.49 / 22.81 / 28.33 / 35.69 / 49.04); the O*NET summary page gives 2024 employment of about 103,100, a 2024—2034 projection of 'average (Average, 3% to 4%)', and about 7,700 projected job openings (that source gives only the category and range rather than a single precise percentage, and this page follows the source wording); the preparation level is Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), the education feedback is 42% less than high school graduation and 24% high school or equivalent and 19% postsecondary certificate (that page shows only these three, totaling 85%), the interest code is RC, and there are 24 tasks; the work context includes standing continuously 92%, continuous use of hands 83%, continuous contact with others 88%, exposure to heights every day 72%, continuous walking or running 78%, face-to-face discussions every day 68%, time pressure every day 52%, decision freedom 'very large' 54%, precision or accuracy 'extremely important' 37%, decisions every day 74%, wearing common protective or safety equipment every day 61%, responsibility for the health and safety of others 'very high responsibility' 45%, competition 'extremely fierce' 43%, continuous climbing of ladders or scaffolds 47%, continuous bending or twisting 52%, minor burns or cuts every day 34%, exposure to hazardous equipment 'every day' 20%, consequences of error 'extremely serious' 30%, continuous kneeling, squatting, bending, or crawling 31%, work hours 'regular' 94%, and automation level 'not automated at all' 55%. Mainland China definition: ceiling works should be carried out in accordance with the current national standard Standard for Construction Quality Acceptance of Building Decoration (GB 50210-2018) and this project's design documents (including material conformity certificates and performance test reports and incoming inspection records and retest reports and concealed works acceptance records and construction records; before installing studs, carry out handover inspection of the room's clear height and opening elevations and the elevations of pipes and equipment and their supports within the ceiling as required by the design; the hanger distance from the end of the main stud must not exceed 300mm and reverse bracing is provided when the hanger length exceeds 1500mm; heavy equipment and equipment with vibration loads must never be installed on the studs of ceiling works; a steel transfer layer is provided when the hanger length exceeds 2500mm); working at height should follow the Technical Code for Safety of Working at Height in Building Construction (JGJ 80) and the Regulations on the Administration of Construction Project Work Safety (State Council Order No. 393) and the Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China, with stable platforms and protection installed and protective equipment such as safety harnesses worn. The above is cited by standard and regulation name and verified key points, and article numbers were not verified one by one. This occupation has no unified access-type occupational qualification in mainland China. Public statistics have not established an occupation-level wage definition corresponding to this occupation, this page preserves the gap as it stands, and industry average wages serve only as a visible industry proxy.
